newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania arrests 149 as opposition parties unite.
newsitem.headline: Albania arrests 149 as opposition parties unite.

text.p: Albania's opposition parties united on Thursday to demand that the government resign as police detained 149 people following a wave of violent protests around the country last weekend.

Seven opposition parties, including the key Socialists and an association of anti-communist dissidents, launched a Forum for Democracy against the ruling right-wing Democrats and promised to investigate the financial scandal which has plunged thousands of Albanians into despair.

The democracy forum was set up by the once-fragmented opposition a day after security forces detained more than 200 people for questioning over clashes and demonstrations over collapsed pyramid investment schemes.
The state prosecutor's office said 149 people had been arrested and charged with violence, theft and damaging public property.

"Through the material evidence and facts we possess, those charged are accused of violent acts against property through theft and destruction, aiming to disrupt public order," deputy prosecutor-general Gani Dizdari said in a statement.
Those detained could face at least 15 years in jail if convicted, the statement said.

Thousands of desperate investors fearing the loss of all their money in the failed pyramid schemes staged protests last weekend, torching government buildings in the southern towns of Berat, Lushnje, Fieri and Vlore.
Despite assurances to investors from President Sali Berisha that they would get some of their money back, a leader of Albania's 1990 anti-communist revolt doubted the troubles would soon be over.

"If the government is not changed, and if people don't get their money back, I do not know what is going to happen but I am very pessimistic," Azem Hajdari, who now heads an independent trade union, said.
"There are no political forces that will be able to keep the crowds under control," he said.
Hajdari co-founded the Democratic Party with Berisha and others, but said he did not rule out working with the new opposition forum to discuss a way out of the crisis.
Hailing the creation of the forum, one of the opposition leaders, Blendi Gonxhe, told a news conference: "It is an historic day...an historic decision to found the forum.
"This is the end of the false dream...of those who thought they could be rich without being free," he said.
Most of the big opposition parties boycotted a general election last May, alleging widespread poll manipulation, intimidation and vote rigging by Berisha's Democrats.
Observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) also reported wide irregularities in the poll -- accusations dismissed by the ruling party.
The Democrats returned to power with an increased majority, winning 122 seats in the 140-member parliament. The Socialists refuse to take up the few seats allocated them.
The pyramid scandal is the worst crisis the Democrats have faced since they toppled the Socialists, successors of the former communist party, in an election in 1992.
